title: Accounting Agents research corpus
mission: A public, read-only research corpus that helps people and agents find, understand, and reuse the information needed to build accounting agents.
coverage_note: Local AA-I122 integration 2026-09-19.1: the verified 2026-09-18.1 corpus is extended with thirteen bounded US tax and filing sources, five named tax-family questions, one synthetic evidence fixture, and five partial or evidence-gap shared-context assessments. The package separates federal income-tax provision and returns, withholding-agent information reporting, method changes, cross-border residence/source/withholding evidence, and the boundary to sales/use/payroll taxes. Existing construction, nonprofit, operating-transaction, management-accounting, ERP, reporting-foundations, and assurance packages remain intact. The corpus retains the existing 96 subsector profiles, 5,952 applicability screenings, and 1,012 individual industry exception reviews. Named answers remain partial or evidence gaps; no whole question family, subsector, or detailed industry is assessed sufficient.
review_note: The 2026-09-19.1 edition is a local AA-I122 integration from base a38de70787ee47653f3e315a3c31f0577b5b9ae2. It adds dated public IRS, US Code, eCFR, and nonauthoritative FASB taxonomy context plus original bounded tax workflows and synthetic arithmetic. It preserves the existing December 2022 Form 3115 source as historical with a successor gap, keeps OECD transfer pricing separate from US residence/source/withholding authority, and does not rewrite Issue 100 construction conflict records or claim publisher clarification. No current consolidated ASC Topic 740 review, taxpayer evidence, treaty conclusion, professional sign-off, empirical agent performance, filing authority, or rights clearance is established. The outgoing 2026-09-18.1 release and prior snapshots remain immutable. This local preparation does not deploy or close AA-I122.
rights_note: Project-created factual metadata is CC0 1.0. Original editorial content is CC BY 4.0. Software is MIT. External source content is not redistributed or licensed by this project; access is not permission for training or reuse.
coverage_priorities: Reverify inherited source URLs, editions, effective dates, supersession, and evidence classifications; keep release-specific checks current.

Deepen real transaction-level and ledger evidence, finance-specific CDC/deletion behavior, ERP completeness and reconciliation examples; documented contracts remain untested here.
Add independent empirical deployment studies, incident and failure reports, and reproducible accounting workflow evidence beyond controlled questions and synthetic datasets.
Resolve dataset-specific and upstream permissions, including TabFormer and the FiFAR/BAF interaction; keep unknown rights unknown.

Deepen construction coverage with current consolidated GAAP review, state-specific tax and public-works rules, contract and job-cost datasets, ERP lineage and professional validation; continue other industry guidance including nonprofit and government implementation.
